summary: RED SIGNAL is a cooperative browser game about designing a Mars mission and then living with your own design decisions. A team of 1–4 players first builds a sample-return mission under real trade-offs: budget, mass, power, data and comms range, choosing a landing site, rocket, relay orbit and equipment such as solar panels, an RTG, a MOXIE oxygen plant and a seismic network. Then they fly it in real time. Astronauts outside see the terrain but not the map; Mission Control inside the lander sees the map and instruments but not the world, so the crew must talk to survive. A repeating seismic signal, the RED SIGNAL, must be located with InSight-style seismology and recovered before the launch window closes, while dust storms, sunset, equipment faults and a solar flare test the design. At the end, a causal report explains which design choice led to which outcome, and the team can redesign and fly again. The game turns abstract mission engineering into a hands-on, team-based learning experience for students aged 14–22 that runs on any laptop with no installation.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

RED SIGNAL is a two-phase cooperative game. In the Mission Design phase the team picks a science goal (signs of ancient life, water ice, or the planet's interior), a landing site (Jezero Crater, Elysium Planitia, Arcadia Planitia), a launch vehicle, a relay orbit and up to six equipment bays. Every choice moves six live gauges (budget, mass, energy, data, comms range, mission time) and a forecast shows when power or oxygen will run out. In the Flight phase the team lives through the mission in real time: astronauts walk, drive a rover, dig samples, explore biomes and lava tubes and deploy seismometers, while Mission Control manages oxygen, power and comms, reads the seismograph and triangulates the epicentre of the repeating RED SIGNAL using range rings, the way InSight located marsquakes. A director adds quakes, meteoroid impacts, dust devils, dust storms, MOXIE faults and a solar flare. The after-action report links outcomes back to design decisions ("you lost power at dusk BECAUSE you chose only solar panels") and offers Redesign / Fly again.

HOW IT WORKS

TypeScript monorepo: a deterministic shared simulation engine, a Node.js + Express + Socket.IO authoritative server (15 Hz), and a React + Phaser 3 client with pixel-art rendering of a 5.6 km procedural valley with five biomes, lava tubes, a rover and oxygen caches. Solo mode runs the same engine fully in the browser with no server. Over 300 automated tests and headless bot players verify every scenario. Multiplayer server hosted on Microsoft Azure; solo version on GitHub Pages.

IMPACT

Designed for classrooms and students aged 14–22: a 4-minute guided training, a 12-minute story mission and a 10-minute free mission; runs on a weak laptop with no installation. The asymmetric roles force real teamwork and communication, and the causal report turns mistakes into lessons about engineering trade-offs.

CREATIVITY

Players do not just design a mission on paper: they personally live through the consequences of their own design in cooperative play with asymmetric information. The detective story is solved with real seismology.

SCIENCE AND HONEST SIMPLIFICATIONS

Mechanics are grounded in NASA missions: InSight (marsquakes, impacts, dust devils, single-station epicentre location), MOXIE (oxygen production limits), Curiosity RAD (the May 2024 solar flare dose), Spirit and Opportunity (soft sand, panel-cleaning events), MRO HiRISE (orbital anomalies), Perseverance (Jezero delta samples) and Mars Sample Return (the ascent vehicle). Time is compressed about 15×, RED SIGNAL itself is fictional, and masses, prices and power are game units that keep real proportions.

Source code: https://github.com/Nurmukasan/Nasa-Space-App-Challange
